name: Abacus
desc_en: Software for tallying election results and calculating seat allocation.
desc_src: Software voor het optellen van verkiezingsuitslagen en berekenen van de zetelverdeling.
short_desc: Software for tallying election results and calculating seat allocation.
long_desc:
Abacus is the new software developed by the Dutch Electoral Council
(Kiesraad) for calculating election results in the Netherlands. It tallies
polling station results and computes the seat allocation.

Abacus replaces the result-consolidation module of the current election
software OSV2020 and will be used for all Dutch elections. The first
version targets the 2026 municipal council elections (GR26).

The software runs as a standalone binary accessible via a web browser on a
local network. The backend is written in Rust, the frontend in
TypeScript/React.

Key design principles are ease-of-use and simplicity. 
From the (dutch) report [Stemmen met vertrouwen](https://www.kiesraad.nl/documenten/2007/09/27/eindrapport-commissie-korthals-altes-stemmen-met-vertrouwen) the 
values integrity, transparency and verifiability are most important.
features: Entry of polling station results using the four-eyes principle
Aggregation of all entered polling station results
Generation of the official record (proces-verbaal) with results

name: Amsterdam Design System
desc_en: An implementation of NL Design System for the City of Amsterdam: reusable components, patterns, and guidelines to build user interfaces.
desc_src: Een implementatie van NL Design System voor gemeente Amsterdam: herbruikbare componenten, patronen en richtlijnen om gebruikersinterfaces te bouwen.
short_desc: An implementation of NL Design System for the City of Amsterdam: reusable components, patterns, and guidelines to build user interfaces.
long_desc:
Amsterdam Design System is an open-source toolkit of ready-made
components that are accessible (WCAG), adaptive, and user-friendly.
Teams reuse them instead of starting from scratch on every project,
saving time and money.

Published as separate packages for CSS, React, and design tokens,
the system lets teams adopt just the parts they need. That makes it
framework-agnostic and suitable for both tailor-made applications and
SaaS applications.

NL Design System’s layered architecture lets other public organisations
reuse these components and apply their own design tokens to tailor them
to their own channels.

The team actively maintains the library, publishes regular releases,
and welcomes contributions.

Het API register biedt een centrale catalogus van APIs die worden aangeboden door de Nederlandse overheid.
Via deze backend-API kunnen APIs worden geregistreerd, opgevraagd en beheerd. Nieuwe registraties worden
automatisch gevalideerd en geïndexeerd in Typesense zodat ze vindbaar zijn via de zoekfunctie op
apis.developer.overheid.nl. De service synchroniseert dagelijks de OpenAPI-specificaties van alle
geregistreerde APIs en genereert automatisch artifacts zoals Postman-collecties.

overheid ontwikkelen. Zij vervult deze rol door het aanbieden van
standaarden, best practices en tools.

Een belangrijke feature van het platform is de API catalogus. Deze maakt
inzichtelijk welke API's er beschikbaar zijn in het publieke landschap.
Tevens kan je hier per API de informatie vinden die je nodig hebt om met

beschikbaar zijn in het publieke landschap. Per project krijgt de
gebruiker inzicht in de vitaliteit van de repository en andere waardevolle
datapunten.

long_desc:
Logboek Dataverwerkingen is a Kotlin library implementing the Dutch government Logboek Dataverwerkingen (LDV) standard for data processing logging. It integrates with Jakarta EE applications via CDI interceptors and exports tracing data to ClickHouse using OpenTelemetry.

The library provides annotation-based tracing via the @Logboek annotation, automatic extraction of W3C Trace Context from HTTP headers, and a request-scoped context for enriching spans with processing details.

desc_en: Signalen is an open source process and task system for governments, that categorizes and routes reports about public space.

short_desc: Signalen is an open source process and task system for governments, that categorizes and routes reports about public space.
long_desc:
Signalen is an open source process and task system for governments, which automatically categorizes and routes reports about public space for processing by the appropriate handler.
The City of Amsterdam receives about 300000 reports about public space every year. From furniture in the garbage to abandoned boats in the canals. More than 1400 civil servants work 24/7 to handle reports in Signalen.
Since the introduction of Signalen, customer satisfaction with the handling of reports in Amsterdam has increased by more than 30 percent.
Signalen software is open source and can be used freely by other governments and municipalities.

desc_en: Experimental personal command centre for saved Mattermost messages - individual research, not production ready.
desc_src: Experimenteel persoonlijk command-centrum voor bewaarde Mattermost-berichten — individueel onderzoek, niet productieklaar.
short_desc: Experimental personal command centre for saved Mattermost messages - individual research, not production ready.
long_desc:
NOTE: Waggle is an individual experiment within the Dutch central government and is known not to meet the requirements and standards the Dutch government sets for production software (BIO/ISO 27001, DPIA/GDPR, WCAG 2.2, NeRDS, Forum Standaardisatie). No formal maintenance, no SLA, single-user single-tenant architecture.
Waggle imports your flagged Mattermost posts into one kanban board with the columns backlog, in progress and done, plus a separate reading list. It has two-way sync with Mattermost (completing a card in Waggle unsaves the post in Mattermost automatically; posts unsaved externally move to done automatically), a rich preview of messages with markdown rendering, attachments, thread context and private notes. Bubble-up to defer cards, a blocked flag for waiting on others, and full keyboard navigation.
The user interface is in Dutch; the documentation is in English.

name: WIM
desc_en: Reusable microservice pipeline that acquires news from public sources, classifies it against advisor profiles (sector/region), and shows it in a dashboard.
desc_src: Herbruikbare microservice-pijplijn die nieuws van publieke bronnen verzamelt, classificeert op adviseursprofiel (sector/regio) en toont in een dashboard.
short_desc: Reusable microservice pipeline that acquires news from public sources, classifies it against advisor profiles (sector/region), and shows it in a dashboard.
long_desc: WIM (Werkgevers Informatie op Maat, "employer information on demand") is a pipeline of reusable microservice building blocks for profile-filtered news monitoring, built at UWV, the Dutch employee insurance agency. The pipeline discovers pages from configured public sources (sitemaps and RSS feeds), classifies them against advisor profiles (sector, region, specialisation), and shows the on-profile matches in a dashboard — so an advisor sees the handful of items that matter to their employers. Everything organisation-specific (sources, classification vocabulary including LLM prompts, profiles) is declarative content rather than code; ADAPTING.md walks another organisation through reusing the pipeline by editing four files. Born as a two-day hackathon build and deliberately published as a working starting point ("open, unless").
features: Source discovery via sitemaps and RSS, declaratively configured
Sector/region classification, offline rules or optional LLM
Advisor profiles with a profile-filtered dashboard
Runs end-to-end with one docker compose up, no API keys required
